open_points.subject: INV-001, INV-017 and PLAT-REG-003 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-001, INV-017, PLAT-REG-003 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal].” The bound check does not establish the complete first-failure order, assignment uniqueness, or rejection of a mismatched returned UUID.
open_points.question: What check must prove every claimed part of INV-001, INV-017 and PLAT-REG-003?
options: Extend the bound check to exercise every ordering, uniqueness and UUID-identity condition
Bind additional checks that collectively assert the omitted conditions
Narrow the claimed invariants
open_points.default_guess: Extend the bound check to cover the omitted conditions.

open_points.subject: INV-004 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-004 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].” The check does not establish indistinguishable payloads or responses and does not show that failures expose no project data.
open_points.question: What observable assertions demonstrate the full concealment required by INV-004?
options: Compare complete failure responses and prove no project data is present
Bind a separate boundary-level concealment check
Narrow INV-004 to the behavior currently checked
open_points.default_guess: Add boundary-level comparisons of complete responses and exposed data.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].” Neither bound check proves both absence of stored current Registry truth and fresh live retrieval across the complete archived read/mutation policy.
open_points.question: Which verification must establish every clause of PLAT-REG-006?
options: Extend one check to inspect persistence and exercise fresh changing Registry answers
Use complementary checks whose stated assertions jointly cover every clause
Narrow PLAT-REG-006
open_points.default_guess: Use a focused linkage check that combines persistence inspection with changing live answers.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-001 verification
open_points.text: “PLAT-REG-001: … no service code generates a project id, the gateway only reads, and every project id the portal stores is one the Registry issued.” The bound Registry linkage check does not prove those universal claims for all generation mechanisms and seeded or stored identifiers.
open_points.question: What enforceable check proves that the Registry is the only creator of every stored project_id?
options: Use an exhaustive architectural or type boundary that makes portal generation impossible and test every storage path
Replace the universal claim with the narrower behavior actually checked
open_points.default_guess: Add an enforceable boundary plus checks over every project_id persistence path.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-005 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:api_transport_financial_policy_registry_gateway_client_portal].” The bound checks do not cover the complete closed failure table or fully exclude cached, client-supplied and fabricated fallback context.
open_points.question: What test matrix must demonstrate every RegistryFailureKind translation and every prohibited fallback?
options: Exercise every table row and each prohibited fallback source
Bind an additional exhaustive gateway check
Narrow PLAT-REG-005
open_points.default_guess: Add an exhaustive table-driven gateway test including all fallback prohibitions.

open_points.subject: INV-031 expense-recognition verification
open_points.text: “an unconfirmed, incomplete, unsupported-version or provider-carrying result is refused at decoding, by create_expense_from_recognition and over HTTP” is claimed by the bound check, but not every named invalid form is exercised at every named boundary.
open_points.question: Must each invalid form be refused independently at decoding, the use case and HTTP, or are some forms impossible past a particular boundary?
options: Test every form at all three named boundaries
State which forms are structurally impossible at later boundaries and test each at every reachable boundary
Reduce the claimed boundary coverage
open_points.default_guess: State reachability explicitly and test every invalid form at every reachable boundary.

open_points.subject: INV-009 grant uniqueness verification
open_points.text: Each separate line says its check “assert[s]” INV-009, but one check covers only service-principal grants and the other only viewer grants.
open_points.question: Is INV-009 established collectively by the two checks, or must each bound check assert both uniqueness rules?
options: Declare one combined Required-tests item binding both checks collectively
Make each check exercise both grant types
Split INV-009 into two invariants
open_points.default_guess: Split INV-009 by grant type or explicitly bind the two checks collectively.

open_points.subject: INV-042 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-042 [witness: verification:project_tracking_audit_writer_sqlite_uow_client_portal].” The check establishes replay behavior but not that a WorkPayment is never a factura/accounting posting or that payments total is derived.
open_points.question: What tests show the non-accounting boundary and derived-total clauses of INV-042?
options: Extend the check to inspect side effects and recompute totals from payments
Bind separate boundary and derivation checks
Split the invariant
open_points.default_guess: Split replay, non-accounting side effects and derived totals into separately verified obligations.

open_points.subject: INV-043 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-043 [witness: verification:photo_management_uow_client_portal].” The check does not establish that visibility-only changes preserve all progress and financial data.
open_points.question: What state comparison demonstrates that every progress and financial fact is unchanged by photo visibility updates?
options: Compare every relevant table and derived view before and after the update
Bind a separate isolation check
Narrow the invariant to named fields
open_points.default_guess: Compare all owning rows and relevant derived views before and after visibility changes.

open_points.subject: INV-037 verification
open_points.text: The two witness lines claim INV-037, but together they do not demonstrate EUR, two-digit semantics, ROUND_HALF_UP and explicit no-conversion behavior across all monetary values and boundaries.
open_points.question: What scope of monetary inputs and derivations must the Required tests cover to justify “all monetary values”?
options: Enumerate and test every monetary boundary and derivation
Define one shared mandatory validator/rounding primitive and verify every path uses it
Narrow the universal invariant
open_points.default_guess: Define shared policy primitives and verify every monetary path is bound to them.

open_points.subject: INV-041 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-041 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].” The check does not assert the exact overall-progress formula or the unavailable result when its denominator is zero.
open_points.question: Which examples and edge cases must prove the exact R9 formula and zero-denominator behavior?
options: Add weighted multi-section, missing-progress and zero-denominator cases
Bind a property test over the formula
Narrow INV-041
open_points.default_guess: Add a property test plus explicit missing-progress and zero-denominator examples.

open_points.subject: INV-044 verification
open_points.text: “a section without a progress record reads completion None and completed work value None” is claimed by the Required-tests item, while the bound check records the completed value as 0.00 rather than asserting None.
open_points.question: What check will demonstrate the changed None semantics before State 2 closes?
options: Update the bound check to require completed_work_value is None
Bind a new check that asserts the changed view contract
Revert the invariant to zero
open_points.default_guess: Update the bound check to require None in both budget and progress views.

open_points.subject: INV-015 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-015 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].” The check does not establish administrator actor provenance, absence of both emails from the audit, or atomic rollback when audit append fails.
open_points.question: What assertions prove every enhanced-audit and atomicity clause of INV-015?
options: Inspect the complete audit record and inject audit failure while comparing all tables
Bind separate provenance, secrecy and atomicity checks
Narrow INV-015
open_points.default_guess: Extend the check with full-record inspection and an audit-failure rollback case.

open_points.subject: INV-005 and INV-006 verification
open_points.text: The authorization, staff-identity and service-identity witness lines claim the full cascade invariants, but omit some revoked credentials and disabled-staff session or credential cases.
open_points.question: Which check or collective test matrix establishes every row of the revocation cascade table?
options: Use one table-driven test covering every revoked object and immediate effect
Declare complementary bindings row by row
Split the invariants by principal or revoked object
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven cascade test with one case per normative row.

open_points.subject: INV-051 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-051 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].” The check covers selected actions but not the entire catalog, actor provenance, or service key_version.
open_points.question: How will every catalog action and every actor-provenance variant be verified?
options: Generate a catalog-driven test for every action and actor kind
Bind action-specific checks that collectively cover the catalog
Narrow INV-051
open_points.default_guess: Generate a catalog-driven matrix including service key_version.

open_points.subject: INV-053 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-053 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].” Additional reason-code cases are checked without proving their records also have result=rejected.
open_points.question: Must every closed reason_code case assert result=rejected in the same record?
options: Assert result and reason_code together for every case
Use a model constraint plus a focused violating-input test
Narrow the claim
open_points.default_guess: Assert both fields together for every closed rejection reason.

open_points.subject: INV-018 verification
open_points.text: The staff-identity witness does not test Unicode casefolding, general syntax rejection, or whitespace refusal required by INV-018.
open_points.question: What input corpus demonstrates the complete normalization and rejection policy?
options: Add Unicode, syntax, internal-whitespace and surrounding-whitespace cases
Bind a property test to the accepted normalizer
Narrow INV-018
open_points.default_guess: Add property-based normalization tests with explicit whitespace and Unicode examples.

open_points.subject: INV-019 verification
open_points.text: The credential-security witness proves preservation of supplied plaintext but not rejection outside 12–128 code points or rejection of the accepted control-character set.
open_points.question: What cases establish every length and control-character rule of INV-019?
options: Test both length boundaries, adjacent failures and every control class
Bind a property test for the accepted validator
Narrow INV-019
open_points.default_guess: Add boundary and control-set property tests.

open_points.subject: INV-022–INV-025 verification
open_points.text: The budget-management witness does not establish producer non-activation, imported-plan immutability, activation rollback atomicity, or exclusive source_key linking without display-name matching.
open_points.question: Which checks must cover the omitted clauses of INV-022 through INV-025?
options: Extend the check with each omitted authorization, failure and linking case
Bind separate focused checks per invariant
Split the combined witness claim
open_points.default_guess: Bind separate focused checks to each invariant and omitted clause.

open_points.subject: INV-020 verification
open_points.text: The snapshot-import witness detects duplicate insertion but does not attempt mutation or deletion of an accepted snapshot, although INV-020 requires immutability and append-only retention.
open_points.question: What test proves accepted snapshots cannot be updated or deleted?
options: Attempt update and delete through every repository or transaction surface
Enforce storage-level immutability and test its constraint
Narrow INV-020
open_points.default_guess: Enforce and test storage-level refusal of update and delete.

open_points.subject: INV-026–INV-028 verification
open_points.text: “no table has a derived-value column” and “no service code deletes or replaces a portal section and no store surface removes one” are universal claims supported only by heuristic scans that can miss violating implementations.
open_points.question: What enforceable evidence proves absence of derived storage and section-removal paths?
options: Define closed schemas and repository interfaces whose structural checks prohibit those features
Use exhaustive behavioral mutation tests plus schema inspection
Narrow the universal claims
open_points.default_guess: Use closed schema and repository-interface checks, supplemented by behavioral tests.

open_points.subject: INV-032 and INV-036 intake verification
open_points.text: The expense-intake witness does not establish amount-correction atomicity or the invariants at later commit points.
open_points.question: Is the intake check intended to assert only creation-time constraints, or the whole lifetime invariants?
options: Limit its binding to creation-time clauses and bind management checks for later mutations
Extend it to execute all management scenarios
Split the invariants by lifecycle stage
open_points.default_guess: Split creation-time and later-mutation obligations and bind each separately.

open_points.subject: INV-032 atomic correction verification
open_points.text: The expense-management witness does not inject a failure between amount correction and allocation replacement, so it does not show that the two changes are atomic at every commit point.
open_points.question: What failure case demonstrates rollback of both amount and allocations?
options: Inject a failure between the two writes and compare all affected rows
Rely on a transaction primitive whose atomicity is separately proven and bind that proof
Narrow the atomicity claim
open_points.default_guess: Inject an intermediate failure and verify the complete prior state remains.

open_points.subject: INV-035 verification
open_points.text: The derived-views witness checks included versus excluded expenses but does not seed an unconfirmed expense, leaving the confirmed-only clause unasserted.
open_points.question: How will the confirmed-only condition be demonstrated?
options: Seed or attempt to seed an unconfirmed expense and prove it cannot enter totals
Prove the model makes persisted unconfirmed expenses impossible and test that boundary
Remove the untestable clause
open_points.default_guess: Prove boundary exclusion and include a defensive derived-view case.

open_points.subject: INV-052 verification
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-052 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].” The check does not attempt update or deletion of audit records or import records.
open_points.question: What test proves both record types are append-only across every storage surface?
options: Attempt update and deletion for each type through transaction and repository surfaces
Enforce storage-level append-only constraints and test them
Narrow INV-052
open_points.default_guess: Add storage-level append-only enforcement and explicit update/delete refusal tests.

open_points.subject: TXN-002 verification
open_points.text: “TXN-001, TXN-002: the transaction guard check” claims that the original exception is re-raised unchanged, but the check compares only its type, not object identity or contents.
open_points.question: What does “original exception unchanged” require the test to compare?
options: Require the exact same exception object by identity
Require equal type, arguments and attached fields
Narrow the rule to type preservation
open_points.default_guess: Require the same exception object to reach the caller.

open_points.subject: TRN-001 verification
open_points.text: The runtime and transport checks observe rejection statuses but do not prove that untrusted-host or oversized-body requests never reach a handler.
open_points.question: What instrumentation demonstrates pre-handler refusal?
options: Install a handler probe and require zero invocations for each rejection
Prove middleware ordering structurally and test it
Narrow TRN-001 to response behavior
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the handler and require it is never called.

open_points.subject: TRN-002 verification
open_points.text: The API transport witness tests a cookie-less viewer read but not foreign-origin viewer sign-out, although the line binds the whole TRN-002 invariant.
open_points.question: Which check must assert both halves of TRN-002?
options: Extend the API transport check with foreign-origin sign-out
Bind the runtime check and API check collectively by clause
Split TRN-002
open_points.default_guess: Add the foreign-origin sign-out case to the API transport check.

open_points.subject: TRN-003 verification
open_points.text: The bound checks cover selected query or synthetic values, not the universal rule that no credential, cookie or secret appears in any log line.
open_points.question: What representative secret sources and logging paths must be exercised to justify TRN-003?
options: Inject unique sentinels into every credential, cookie and secret input and inspect all emitted logs
Enforce centralized structural redaction and verify every logger uses it
Narrow TRN-003
open_points.default_guess: Combine centralized redaction enforcement with sentinel tests across all secret-bearing inputs.

open_points.subject: clock invariant identity
open_points.text: A28 declares “All portal-owned event timestamps written by one operation…” without a stable invariant identifier, while the State 2 readiness assessment says “Every invariant has a stable ledger id” and the carry-forward rule requires each invariant's test binding.
open_points.question: What stable identifier names the A28 clock invariant for later contracts and witness resolution?
options: Assign a new clock invariant id
Declare that the unnumbered invariant is outside the invariant ledger and amend readiness/carry-forward text
open_points.default_guess: Assign a stable clock invariant id.

open_points.subject: clock-policy verification
open_points.text: “A test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades, bootstrap) that its written timestamps, other than audit occurred_at, are one instant.” The bound checks cover only selected operations and do not prove all timestamp equality, TTL derivation, source-time preservation, or exclusive use of the named clock source.
open_points.question: What tests establish every clause of the clock invariant and the one-source policy?
options: Test every timestamp-writing operation plus TTL and source-supplied cases, and prohibit direct host-clock reads structurally
Narrow the invariant to the operations currently checked
Split clock-source, equality, TTL and source-preservation obligations
open_points.default_guess: Split the obligations and add structural enforcement against direct host-clock reads.

open_points.subject: configuration invariant verification
open_points.text: “The existence of every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound is invariant” is bound to checks that cover only selected viewer-entry and binary settings, not every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound.
open_points.question: What closed inventory and test demonstrate that every required configuration class exists?
options: Enumerate every required setting and test presence, type and startup behavior for each
Narrow the invariant to the settings currently listed and checked
Bind additional component-specific checks
open_points.default_guess: Create a closed inventory and a table-driven configuration test.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 public advisory verification
open_points.text: The Required-tests item says the image is judged “against a public advisory snapshot,” but the bound release-gate check does not validate that the supplied snapshot originates from a public advisory source.
open_points.question: What evidence makes an advisory snapshot an authenticated or otherwise verifiable public-database snapshot rather than arbitrary input?
options: Validate signed provenance and source metadata from an allowed public database
Fetch the snapshot only through a fixed Factory-controlled public source
Remove “public” from the invariant and rule
open_points.default_guess: Require verifiable provenance from a Factory-approved public advisory source.
